'''Irina Petrovna Beletskaya''' ({{langx|ru|Ири́на Петро́вна Беле́цкая}}; born 10 March 1933) is a Soviet and Russian professor of chemistry at [[Moscow State University]]. She specializes in [[organometallic chemistry]] and its application to problems in [[organic chemistry]]. She is best known for her studies on aromatic reaction mechanisms, as well as work on [[carbanion]] acidity and reactivity.<ref name="ArkivicTribute">{{Cite journal|date=Jun 10, 2007|title=A Tribute to Prof. Irina P. Beletskaya|url=https://content.arkat-usa.org/ARKIVOC/JOURNAL_CONTENT/manuscripts/2008/IB-1430FT%20as%20published%20mainmanuscript.pdf|journal=[[Arkivoc]]|volume=2008|issue=iv|pages=1–7}}</ref> She developed some of the first methods for carbon-carbon bond formation using [[palladium]] or [[nickel]] catalysts, and extended these reactions to work in aqueous media. She also helped to open up the chemistry of [[Organolanthanide chemistry|organolanthanides]].

== Academic career ==
Beletskaya was born in Leningrad ([[Saint Petersburg|St. Petersburg]], Russia) in 1933.<ref name="ArkivicTribute" /> She graduated from the Department of Chemistry of Lomonosov [[Moscow State University]] in 1955 where she focused her undergraduate research on organoarsenic chemistry.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Ananikov |first1=Valentine |last2=Gevorgyan |first2=Vladimir |last3=Moberg |first3=Christina |last4=Suginome |first4=Michinori |last5=Trzeciak |first5=Anna |date=2023-09-25 |title=Irina Beletskaya: Chemistry Excellence in Scientific Endeavors |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.organomet.3c00352 |journal=Organometallics |language=en |volume=42 |issue=18 |pages=2415–2425 |doi=10.1021/acs.organomet.3c00352 |issn=0276-7333|url-access=subscription }}</ref> She obtained the Candidate of Chemistry (analogous to Ph.D.) degree in 1958.<ref name="dx.doi.org">{{Cite journal|date=2007-06-10|title=A Tribute to Prof. Irina P. Beletskaya|journal=Arkivoc|volume=2008|issue=4|pages=1–7|doi=10.3998/ark.5550190.0009.401|doi-access=free|last1=Schantl|first1=Joachim|hdl=2027/spo.5550190.0009.401|hdl-access=free}}</ref> For this degree she investigated electrophilic substitution reactions. More specifically, she explored the influence of ammonia on a-bromomercurophenylacetic acid reactions.<ref name=":0" /> In 1963 she received her Dr.Sci. degree from the same institution.<ref name="Organoelement">{{cite web|url=https://www.chem.msu.ru/eng/chairs2/organic/welcome.html|title=Division of Organic Chemistry|date=April 14, 2006|publisher=[[Moscow State University]]|access-date=2007-09-10}}</ref> In 1970 she became a Full Professor of Chemistry at [[Moscow State University]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Beletskaya|first1=Irina|last2=Tyurin|first2=Vladimir S.|last3=Tsivadze|first3=Aslan Yu.|last4=Guilard|first4=Roger|last5=Stern|first5=Christine|date=2009-05-13|title=Supramolecular Chemistry of Metalloporphyrins|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=109|issue=5|pages=1659–1713|doi=10.1021/cr800247a|pmid=19301872|issn=0009-2665}}</ref> where she currently serves as head of the [https://www.chem.msu.su/eng/lab/orgcomp.html Organoelement Chemistry Laboratory]. Beletskaya was elected a corresponding member of the Academy of Science of USSR in 1974. In 1992 she became a full member (academician) of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="ArkivicTribute" /> Between 1991 and 1993 she served as president of the Division of Organic Chemistry of [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry|IUPAC]].<ref name="ArkivicTribute" /> Until 2001 she served on the IUPAC Committee on Chemical Weapons Destruction Technology (CWDT).<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pEtnBgAAQBAJ|title=Women Scientists: Reflections, Challenges, and Breaking Boundaries|last=Hargittai|first=Magdolna|date=2015-03-04|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=9780199359998|language=en}}</ref> She is editor-in chief of the [https://link.springer.com/journal/11178 Russian Journal of Organic Chemistry].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/chemistry/organic+chemistry/journal/11178?detailsPage=editorialBoard&token=prtst0416p|title=Russian Journal of Organic Chemistry (Editorial Board)|website=springer.com|access-date=2016-04-19|archive-date=2019-03-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190323130905/https://www.springer.com/chemistry/organic%2Bchemistry/journal/11178%3FdetailsPage%3DeditorialBoard%26token%3Dprtst0416p|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Beletskaya initially researched the reaction mechanisms of organic reactions, focusing on compounds with metal-carbon bonds.<ref name=":0" /> Her research included Grignard-like reactions and lanthanide complexes in the context of catalysts. She and Prof. O. Reutov worked on electrophilic reactions at saturated carbon. She also investigated the reaction mechanisms of organometallic compounds. She also researched carbanion reactivity, emphasizing the reactivity and structure of ion pairs.<ref name="dx.doi.org" />  Once more advanced in her career, Beltskaya focused more on [[transition metal]] catalysts and developing economically favorable catalysts. Currently, she serves as the head of the Laboratory of Organoelement Compounds within the Department of Chemistry at Moscow State University, where she has concentrated her research on [[carbon dioxide]] utilization and its utility in renewable energy and reactions with epoxides.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Shul’pin |first1=Georgiy Borisovich |last2=Adams |first2=Richard D. |date=2018-07-15 |title=Biosketch for Irina P. Beletskaya |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022328X18303449 |journal=Journal of Organometallic Chemistry |series=Special Issue dedicated to Prof. Irina Beletskaya |volume=867 |pages=2–3 |doi=10.1016/j.jorganchem.2018.05.011 |issn=0022-328X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Research contributions ==
Beletskaya is known for her foundational contributions to organometallic chemistry and as one of the first prominent female chemists. Her work helped pave the way for women in Russia to participate in the scientific community.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Beletskaya |first=I.P. |date=2016 |title=Is It Easy to Be a Woman in Science? |url=https://chemistry-europe.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1002/chem.201505051?src=getftr |journal=Chemistry - A European Journal |volume=22 |issue=11 |pages=3531–3532|doi=10.1002/chem.201505051 |pmid=26880132 }}</ref> Her pioneering role in organometallic synthesis has laid an essential foundation for future organic chemists. Her work advocating for rare-earth elements in organic chemistry led to the publication of many new textbooks, changing how organic chemistry is taught everywhere.<ref name=":1" /> The current field of organic chemists does not always see the need to include other elements in the study of organic chemistry, as it is all carbon-based.<ref name=":0" /> Beletskaya’s work helps to expand the use of precious metals in organic reactions.
